issues: No integrity problems. The diff changes one hyperparameter, MATRIX_LR (Muon learning rate), from 0.04 to 0.05. It doesn't touch how val_bpb is measured, the data, the seed lines, the evaluation call, the prepare.py import line or the summary printing.
No bugs that would make the result meaningless. A 25% higher matrix LR is an ordinary tuning change.

The numbers and the decision agree. The candidate scored 1.0783 against an incumbent mean of 1.0757, so it is 0.0026 worse (lower is better). A negative z of -0.390 points the same way, and reject is the right call.
I couldn't recompute z: the harness gave no per-run incumbent values or standard deviation. The reported z implies a noise scale of about 0.0026/0.39 ≈ 0.0067. That is plausible but can't be checked.

Weak evidence: there is only 1 candidate run against 2 incumbent runs. The gap is well within noise, so this run neither shows that MATRIX_LR=0.05 is worse nor that it is better. Rejecting is still fine, since there is no evidence of a gain.
